h1: Bay Hotel Srinakarin — Spacious Rooms, Budget Price in the Srinakarin Area Near BTS
intro: If you want a Srinakarin-area base with roomy, affordable rooms and easy BTS access into the city, Bay Hotel Srinakarin is a long-standing favourite among budget-minded travellers. This 3-star, 159-room hotel sits on Srinakarin Road in Samrong Nuea, Mueang Samut Prakan — near BTS Si Iam and Seacon Square, with free parking, a gym, a spa and two restaurants. Rooms start from approx. ฿700/night, and it holds an 8.0 score from over 270 real guest reviews on Trip.com. It's an older property that still offers value in its own way.

body.html: The main reason people choose Bay Hotel Srinakarin is its spacious rooms at a low price. The Superior and Deluxe rooms here run 32–36 square metres — larger than many similarly priced hotels on Bangkok's east side. Guests often note a wide bed, a desk, two chairs and plenty of room to move, rather than the cramped feel of typical budget rooms.

The location is on Srinakarin Road in the Samrong Nuea area — about 600 metres from BTS Si Iam, within walking distance, with the Sukhumvit line running straight into central Bangkok. Seacon Square, a large mall, is close by, along with plenty of roadside restaurants on Srinakarin. It's about a 25-minute drive (roughly 21 km) to Suvarnabhumi Airport, so it works as a pre-flight base, though it isn't airport-adjacent like the Bang Phli hotels.

Facilities are adequate for the price. There's generous free parking, a gym, a spa, two restaurants, a cafe and a karaoke room. There's no swimming pool — worth knowing if you're hoping to swim. The free parking is something self-drivers praise often, since parking in the Srinakarin area is scarce and pricey.
"The room was really spacious for the price, the front-desk staff were friendly, you can walk to the BTS, and free parking made it easy. The hotel is a bit old but genuinely good value."

The thing to keep in mind is the age of the building and decor. The hotel opened back in 2009, and a number of reviews mention old furniture, patches of peeling wall paint and squeaky floors in some rooms. A few guests have reported pest issues such as cockroaches — worth checking your room at check-in and asking to switch if you're unhappy. This isn't a sleek new hotel; it's an older property kept up reasonably well at a budget price.

Another point reviewers raise is inconsistency between rooms. Some rooms have been renovated and others are still original, so guests have varied experiences — some get a fresher, clean room, others an older one. If you can, ask for a renovated room when booking or at check-in, and choose a higher floor to avoid noise from the busy Srinakarin Road.

Overall, Bay Hotel Srinakarin holds an 8.0 out of 10 on Trip.com from over 270 real guest reviews. It's a sensible pick for budget travellers who want a roomy space, rely mainly on the BTS, or drive in and need free parking. Prices start around ฿700 and climb with the season into the low thousands for a Deluxe room. If you can accept the building's age and don't need a pool or a polished finish, it offers solid value in the Srinakarin area.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Bay Hotel Srinakarin

faq.q: Where is Bay Hotel Srinakarin, and is it near the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is on Srinakarin Road in Samrong Nuea, Mueang Samut Prakan. It's about 600 metres from BTS Si Iam (Sukhumvit line) — within walking distance — and close to Seacon Square, BITEC Bangna and Mega Bangna. It's about a 25-minute drive to Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: How much does Bay Hotel Srinakarin cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. ฿700/night for a Superior Double. Options range from Superior Twin (32 sqm) to Deluxe rooms (36 sqm) and renovated rooms. Rates climb with the season into the low thousands — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Bay Hotel Srinakarin — are they old?
faq.a: The big plus is spacious 32–36 sqm rooms, larger than similarly priced hotels. That said, the building opened back in 2009, and some furniture and walls are dated, with rooms varying between old and renovated. It's best to request a renovated room and inspect it at check-in.

faq.q: Does Bay Hotel Srinakarin have parking and a pool?
faq.a: There's generous free parking, which self-drivers praise often, since parking in the Srinakarin area is scarce. There's also a gym, spa, two restaurants and karaoke. But there's no swimming pool — worth knowing if you're hoping to swim.

faq.q: Who is Bay Hotel Srinakarin best for?
faq.a: It suits budget travellers who want a roomy space and rely mainly on the BTS, or self-drivers who need free parking. It works for an unhurried stay before a Suvarnabhumi flight, but it's less suited to anyone wanting a sleek new hotel or a swimming pool.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Bay Hotel Srinakarin to Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faq.a: It's roughly 21 km, about a 25-minute drive depending on traffic. The hotel offers a paid airport shuttle. Because it isn't airport-adjacent like the Bang Phli hotels, allow enough travel time for very early flights.
